applicability: A required ordering is not visible as a buffer overlap.
A consumer must wait on a loop's worth of producers or on a producer created inside a manual scope.
A non-critical sibling is taking a speculative early-dispatch window that a critical-path task needs.
directions: Capture a producer with `with pl.at(level=pl.Level.CORE_GROUP, name_hint='producer') as first:` and declare the consumer with `deps=[first]`.
Use `gate = pl.system.task_dummy(deps=[tid_a, tid_b])` to join producers, or `pl.system.task_dummy(deps=[])` as a placeholder when no fused-path producer exists.
Use `late = pl.system.task_dummy(deps=[rms_tid])` to delay one non-critical consumer by a dispatch hop.
Hoist `pl.array.create(N, pl.TASK_ID)` outside a manual scope and use `deps=[down_tids[k] for k in range(N)]` for the fan-in if the whole-array form does not produce the expected edges.
effects: Explicit edges recover correctness or concurrency that inference cannot see, but each edge adds scheduler bookkeeping and can serialize independent work.
A dummy join reduces multiple handles to one but adds a dispatch hop.
A deliberate delay can protect a critical task's early-dispatch window, but it costs one dispatch and is only justified by before/after evidence.
invariants: `deps=` entries must be TaskId scalars, arrays, or accepted sentinels; tensor arguments use `no_dep_args`/`pl.no_dep`, not `deps=`.
A TaskId names one task. For an SPMD fan-out it names the whole launch, so a consumer cannot wait on one logical block.
`pl.system.task_dummy` is a parser construct and is not callable outside a decorated body.
A dummy with `deps=[c_tid]` adds a hop after `c`; a dummy with `deps=[]` is ready immediately. Adding the wrong one changes the schedule for a different reason.
The registered documents conflict on whether non-`as tid` `pl.spmd` forms accept `deps=`; use the `as tid` spelling until locally verified.
principle: A `pl.at` scope can be named with `as tid`; `pl.submit` and `pl.spmd_submit` return a result plus a producer TaskId. `deps=` accepts TaskIds, and a fan-in can be passed as an array of `pl.TASK_ID` created with `pl.array.create(N, TASK_ID)`. When a TaskId array must cross a manual-scope boundary, hoist the array into orchestration scope before the manual region so a later outside consumer can read it. Some models rely on a per-index list of TaskIds rather than passing the whole array; both spellings are documented, and the hoisted-across-scope case is the one where the per-index form is known to work. `pl.system.task_dummy(deps=[...])` is a join with no kernel work: it collapses several producers into one handle. With `deps=[]` it is a ready-on-submit placeholder that satisfies a shared signature. With one real producer plus a hop it deliberately delays a consumer, which is useful when a non-critical sibling resolves at the same instant as a critical one. A dummy has no `allow_early_resolve` parameter and accepts only `deps=`. Explicit edges are ordering, not a lifetime extension in the L3 host path: a host `deps=[producer]` lowers to `add_dep_wait` so the consumer waits without extending the producer's resource lifetime.
questions: Whether a hoisted whole-array `deps=` is normalized to the same edges as the per-index list in every outliner path.
risks: Adding a dummy to the shared producer rather than to the non-critical sibling, delaying both consumers.
Adding an unflagged dummy to the critical consumer itself, making it structurally ineligible for the window it needed.
Assuming a whole-array `deps=` works identically to a per-index list across a hoisted manual-scope boundary.
Treating `deps=` as a replacement for correct buffer directions; it only adds edges.
summary: `deps=` names producer TaskIds so a consumer waits on work that may have no buffer overlap. TaskIds can be captured from `pl.at`, `submit`, `spmd`, or `spmd_submit`, collected in arrays, joined with `pl.system.task_dummy`, or used to delay a non-critical consumer by one hop.
title: Explicit Edges, TaskIds, Fan-In Arrays, and Dummy Tasks
